SUBMISSION PROCESS TIMELINE

The process begins with submission of the proposal to AELR (15-day review begins).

On the 16th day after submission to AELR, the proposal becomes available to submit to DSD.

Submission for publication in the Maryland Register is a separate step; the date of publication is based on the date of submission to DSD--NOT to AELR.

The agency must wait 45 days after publication of the proposal in the Register before adopting the proposal (the first 30 days constitutes the public comment period).

As early as the 46th day (and until up to one year) after publication of the proposal, the agency may adopt the regulations by publication of a notice of final action in the Register. The date of publication is determined by the submission date of the final.

Unless the agency chooses a later date, the regulatory changes proposed and adopted become effective 10 days after publication of the final action in the Register.

  * Continue to be necessary for public interest;
  * Continue to be supported by statutory authority and judicial opinions;
  * Are obsolete or otherwise appropriate for amendment or repeal;
  * Continue to be effective in accomplishing the intended purposes of the regulations.

Regulations proposed but not yet adopted are published biweekly in the Maryland Register, available by print or electronic subscription from the Division of State Documents. In COMAR Online, you view regulations individually, and not as part of the larger chapter designation.
